title: Urban infrastructure and fossil fuel industrial legacy drive US data center siting
methods: GIS overlay with metro/micropolitan statistical areas
data_sources: IRA Energy Community data layers (DOE/NETL EDX)
US Census TIGER/Line and CBSA definitions
BLS OEWS and QCEW county-MSA-CSA crosswalk
SLOPE county energy consumption data viewer

data_scope.spatial_coverage: United States, analyzed at county and metropolitan/micropolitan statistical area (CBSA) level
data_scope.headline_statistic: 97.5% of data centers located in metropolitan or micropolitan statistical areas
data_scope.facility_count: not stated in the openly accessible text (primary dataset is commercial and license-restricted)
data_scope.input_vintages: approximately 2022-2025 (EVI 2022; eGRID/FEMA NRI/EIA/ACS/OEWS 2023; DataCenterMap and several Census/BLS layers 2025)
data_scope.availability: processed data and code open at github.com/dynamicalsystemslaboratory/Data-centers-siting-across-U.S.-cities; primary commercial dataset restricted

core_conclusion: US data centers are overwhelmingly urban - 97.5% sit within metropolitan or micropolitan statistical areas - refuting the 'rural cloud expansion' narrative. Siting is driven primarily by the nameplate capacity of local power plants, and secondarily by broadband quality, retired coal plants, IT employment and natural-hazard risk. Because facilities rely on local generation, they inherit state-level energy mixes and amplify geographic contrasts in sustainability, while population-based projections indicate growth will reinforce existing urban hierarchies rather than decentralize - a path-dependent evolution tied to fossil-fuel industrial legacy.
why_it_matters: Replaces a policy-shaping myth ('AI is moving to the countryside') with a national statistic; identifies electricity generation capacity, not land or labor, as the dominant siting driver; documents fossil-fuel lock-in via retired coal plants and IRA energy-community geography; reframes data centers as an urban livability and energy-justice problem; and forecasts concentration rather than diffusion of grid, water and land stress.
why_nature: Overturns a prevailing narrative with national evidence; joins infrastructure, energy systems and distributional equity in one frame, matching Nature Cities' cross-cutting urban-systems remit; is immediately policy-actionable amid state data-center legislation and interconnection debates; frames path dependence as a transferable urban mechanism; and pairs forward-looking SSP scenarios with an openly released reproducible pipeline.
added_value_to_my_research: MGWR + SHAP refit of the global negative-binomial siting model -> map of elasticities for explainable spatial prediction
Population-weighted exposure surface around facilities -> reverse-2SFCA formulation for disamenity burden and environmental health
Invert the broadband arrow with a before/after panel -> latency-decay 2SFCA metric for telehealth and digital access
Agent-based / physics-informed graph simulator of grid-demography co-evolution -> generalizes my EV charging efficiency-equity optimization
Facility opening-date panel with spatiotemporal KDE, survival models and spatial entropy -> transferable legacy-conversion lag template
